out_of_scope_sections.reason: Per-platform overview pages; principle extraction covers the five guidance sections only.

classes.universal: The principle holds on the web and on other platforms without translating an Apple mechanism.
classes.adapt: The goal is universal, but HIG expresses it through an Apple mechanism or value that must be translated to a named web or cross-platform counterpart.
classes.apple-specific: The guidance depends on Apple hardware, system rendering, licensing, or brand assets and must not become a web default.

principles.statement: Give every interactive control a hit area and surrounding spacing large enough that a person with limited dexterity reliably activates the intended control.
principles.class_reason: HIG states its minimum in Apple points per platform; on the web the floor is WCAG 2.5.8 (24 by 24 CSS px or equivalent spacing), with 2.5.5 as the enhanced target.
principles.verification_question: Does every pointer target meet 24 by 24 CSS px, or have enough spacing that a 24 px circle around it touches no other target?

principles.statement: Let people enlarge text without losing content, controls, or reading order.
principles.class_reason: HIG frames this through Dynamic Type; the web equivalents are browser zoom, text-only zoom, and relative units, verified against WCAG resize and reflow criteria.
principles.verification_question: At 200% text size and at a 320 CSS px wide viewport, is every piece of content and every control still reachable without two-dimensional scrolling?

principles.statement: Keep text, icons, and control boundaries distinguishable from their background in every supported appearance.
principles.class_reason: Contrast need comes from human vision, not from a platform; both HIG and WCAG require measurable minimums.
principles.verification_question: Do body text, large text, and essential non-text indicators meet 4.5:1, 3:1, and 3:1 in light, dark, and increased-contrast states?

principles.statement: Never make color the only carrier of status, meaning, or interactivity; pair it with text, shape, or position.
principles.class_reason: Color-vision differences exist on every platform.
principles.verification_question: If the screen is rendered in grayscale, can every status, error, selected item, and link still be identified?

principles.statement: Expose a meaningful name, role, and current state for every control and informative image to assistive technology.
principles.class_reason: HIG names VoiceOver; the requirement is the same for any screen reader on any platform.
principles.verification_question: Does a screen reader announce a specific name, the correct role, and the current state for each control in the flow?

principles.statement: Offer text-based and described alternatives such as captions, transcripts, and audio description for audio and video content.
principles.class_reason: People who cannot hear or see the media exist regardless of device.
principles.verification_question: Does every prerecorded video with speech have synchronized captions, and is essential visual information described?

principles.statement: When a cue is delivered by sound or vibration, deliver the same information through a visible channel too.
principles.class_reason: Sensory redundancy is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Can a person with sound off and no vibration still notice every alert and confirmation?

principles.statement: Keep common actions reachable with simple single-pointer input and provide an alternative for any path-based, multi-finger, or drag gesture.
principles.class_reason: Motor limits apply to every touch and pointer surface.
principles.verification_question: Can every gesture-driven action also be done with a single tap or click, without dragging?

principles.statement: Make the whole experience operable with a keyboard alone, with a visible focus indicator and no traps.
principles.class_reason: HIG pairs this with Full Keyboard Access and Switch Control; keyboard operability is the shared base for all such technologies.
principles.verification_question: Can the main task be completed using only Tab, Shift+Tab, arrow keys, Enter, Space, and Escape, with focus always visible?

principles.statement: Make the spoken name of each control match its visible label so voice-input users can target it by saying what they see.
principles.class_reason: HIG frames this through Voice Control; on the web it maps to the accessible name containing the visible label text.
principles.verification_question: Does each control's accessible name start with, or contain, its visible label text?

principles.statement: Avoid interface elements that expire on a timer; when a limit is unavoidable, let people extend or turn it off.
principles.class_reason: Cognitive and motor differences make fixed time limits exclusionary everywhere.
principles.verification_question: Can every timed element be paused, extended, or disabled before it expires?

principles.statement: Let people stop moving or blinking content and avoid flashes that can trigger seizures.
principles.class_reason: Photosensitivity and vestibular risk are physiological, not platform-bound.
principles.verification_question: Does any content flash more than three times per second, and can every auto-moving element be paused?

principles.statement: Assign each color one meaning and keep that meaning stable across the product.
principles.class_reason: Consistent semantics reduce learning cost on any platform.
principles.verification_question: Is any one color used for two unrelated meanings, such as both success and selection?

principles.statement: Check every color pairing in each appearance the product ships, including high-contrast modes, and under varied ambient lighting.
principles.class_reason: Display conditions vary across all devices.
principles.verification_question: Has each foreground/background pair been measured in every appearance the product ships?

principles.statement: Reference colors through named semantic roles that resolve per appearance, rather than hard-coding literal values.
principles.class_reason: HIG relies on Apple dynamic system colors; on the web use role-named custom properties, CSS system colors, and appearance media queries.
principles.verification_question: Can the appearance change without editing any literal color value inside component code?

principles.statement: Consider that color connotations differ across cultures and regions before attaching meaning to a hue.
principles.class_reason: Cultural interpretation is independent of platform.
principles.verification_question: Has the color meaning been checked for each target locale?

principles.statement: Tinting rules for Apple's system glass material describe an Apple-rendered surface and are not a web default.
principles.class_reason: The material is drawn by Apple's system frameworks; imitating it on the web is out of bounds under this domain's no-imitation boundary.
principles.verification_question: Does the web adaptation avoid recreating Apple's system glass and instead use a verified opaque or tonal surface?

principles.statement: Follow the person's system-wide light or dark preference by default.
principles.class_reason: HIG discourages an app-only appearance switch; on the web honor prefers-color-scheme and color-scheme, and treat any site-level override as a deliberate product decision.
principles.verification_question: With no saved preference, does the page render in the operating system's current appearance?

principles.statement: Make content, images, and icons legible and well-balanced in both light and dark appearances.
principles.class_reason: Any product offering two appearances must verify both.
principles.verification_question: Do all text, icons, and full-color images keep required contrast and remain recognizable in both appearances?

principles.statement: Avoid pure, glaring white backgrounds in dark contexts; dim large bright surfaces so they do not overpower nearby content.
principles.class_reason: Glare in low light is a display property, not a platform rule.
principles.verification_question: Does any large bright surface appear inside the dark appearance without being dimmed?

principles.statement: Design each interface icon around one simplified, recognizable concept and keep the icon family visually consistent.
principles.class_reason: Icon legibility principles are shared across design systems.
principles.verification_question: Can people name the action of each icon without its label, and do all icons share stroke weight and style?

principles.statement: Give every icon-only control a text alternative that names its action.
principles.class_reason: Assistive technology needs a name for any non-text control.
principles.verification_question: Does every icon-only button have an accessible name that describes the action, not the picture?

principles.statement: Prefer vector formats for interface icons and align them optically with adjacent text.
principles.class_reason: Resolution independence and optical alignment apply to every rendering surface.
principles.verification_question: Are interface icons delivered as vector assets and vertically aligned with their labels at every text size?

principles.statement: Deliver images that stay sharp at every display density the product supports, preferring vector art for flat graphics.
principles.class_reason: HIG names Apple scale factors; on the web use responsive image sources, vector formats, and verified density descriptors.
principles.verification_question: On a high-density display, is every bitmap served at sufficient resolution without oversized downloads?

principles.statement: Verify artwork on real target displays, not only in design tools.
principles.class_reason: Color profiles and densities differ across physical screens.
principles.verification_question: Was the artwork reviewed on at least one physical device per target display class?

principles.statement: Write in plain language, define specialist terms, and avoid idioms that do not translate.
principles.class_reason: Comprehension and translation needs are universal.
principles.verification_question: Does any user-facing string contain an undefined term of art or a colloquialism?

principles.statement: Refer to people respectfully, use people-first wording about disability, and avoid assumptions about identity.
principles.class_reason: Respectful communication is independent of platform.
principles.verification_question: Does any copy assume gender, family structure, or ability where it does not need to?

principles.statement: Choose imagery and examples that represent a broad range of people and do not exclude people with disabilities.
principles.class_reason: Representation concerns apply to every product surface.
principles.verification_question: Do illustrations and sample data represent a range of people rather than one default?

principles.statement: Order content by importance so the most relevant information comes first in both visual and reading order.
principles.class_reason: Reading and focus order must match the visual hierarchy on any platform.
principles.verification_question: Does the DOM and focus order present the primary content and action before secondary material?

principles.statement: Group related items and use alignment and indentation to express hierarchy.
principles.class_reason: Proximity and alignment are general perception principles.
principles.verification_question: Are grouped items also grouped semantically, for example with a list, fieldset, or section heading?

principles.statement: Reveal secondary detail on demand rather than showing everything at once.
principles.class_reason: Reducing upfront complexity is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Is secondary detail hidden behind a labeled control that exposes its expanded state?

principles.statement: Base layout changes on the space actually available, keeping functionality the same and changes recognizable as size changes.
principles.class_reason: HIG uses Apple size classes; on the web use intrinsic layout, container queries, and viewport breakpoints only for viewport-level shells.
principles.verification_question: When the container narrows from roomy to tight, does every function remain available in a recognizable arrangement?

principles.statement: Make controls visually distinguishable from the content they act on.
principles.class_reason: Affordance clarity is shared across design systems.
principles.verification_question: Can a first-time viewer tell which elements are interactive without hovering?

principles.statement: Keep controls and essential content out of regions that hardware or system interface may cover.
principles.class_reason: HIG names Apple safe areas and camera housings; on the web use env(safe-area-inset-*) with viewport-fit and test on devices with display cutouts.
principles.verification_question: On a device with a display cutout or home indicator, is any control or essential text obscured?

principles.statement: Apple's translucent system materials, including Liquid Glass, are rendered by Apple frameworks and are not a pattern to recreate on the web.
principles.class_reason: Recreating the visual signature would be platform imitation; the web counterpart decision is an opaque or tonal surface verified for contrast.
principles.verification_question: Does the adaptation avoid backdrop-blur imitation of Apple system materials as a default surface?

principles.statement: When content sits over any translucent or blurred surface, verify legibility against the worst-case background, not the typical one.
principles.class_reason: HIG relies on system vibrancy to keep text legible; on the web no such guarantee exists, so contrast must be measured on real backgrounds.
principles.verification_question: Has text over every translucent layer been measured against the lightest and darkest content that can scroll beneath it?

principles.statement: Use motion only where it communicates status, feedback, or spatial relationship, and keep it from dominating the task.
principles.class_reason: Purposeful motion is a shared principle across HIG and Material.
principles.verification_question: Can each animation be justified by the information it conveys?

principles.statement: Make motion optional and provide an equivalent non-moving presentation when people reduce motion.
principles.class_reason: HIG ties this to the Reduce Motion setting; on the web honor prefers-reduced-motion and keep the same content available.
principles.verification_question: With reduced motion enabled, is all content and state still conveyed without non-essential movement?

principles.statement: Keep feedback motion short and precise, and let people interrupt or cancel it without waiting.
principles.class_reason: Responsiveness and control are platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Can new input interrupt any running transition without a locked or jumping state?

principles.statement: Avoid animating interactions that people repeat many times in a session.
principles.class_reason: Repeated animation becomes friction on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Is any high-frequency action, such as typing or toggling, gated by an animation?

principles.statement: Collect only data the feature genuinely needs and explain how it is used.
principles.class_reason: Data minimization is a general privacy principle and a legal expectation in many regions.
principles.verification_question: Can each requested data item be tied to a specific feature that would fail without it?

principles.statement: Request access to sensitive resources at the moment a feature needs it, with copy that explains why, rather than at first launch.
principles.class_reason: Contextual permission requests apply to web permission prompts as much as native ones.
principles.verification_question: Is every permission request triggered by a person's action on the feature that needs it?

principles.statement: Never place a screen before a system permission prompt that pressures, confuses, or misrepresents the choice.
principles.class_reason: Deceptive consent design is harmful on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Does any pre-permission screen offer only one path, hide the decline option, or misdescribe the system prompt?

principles.statement: Offer authentication that does not rely only on a memorized password, such as passkeys.
principles.class_reason: HIG names keychain and Apple sign-in; on the web the counterparts are WebAuthn passkeys and password-manager-friendly fields.
principles.verification_question: Can a person sign in without transcribing or memorizing a secret, for example with a passkey or autofill?

principles.statement: Mirror interface direction for right-to-left scripts, flipping controls that express reading order or progress.
principles.class_reason: Script direction support is required for any localized product.
principles.verification_question: With dir=rtl, do navigation order, progress controls, and back/forward affordances flip while layout stays intact?

principles.statement: Keep the digits within a number in their natural order and keep icons that depict physical direction or real objects unflipped.
principles.class_reason: Number and object semantics do not change with script direction.
principles.verification_question: In right-to-left mode, are numbers, clocks, media play icons, and photographs left unmirrored?

principles.statement: Align each paragraph according to its own language, not the surrounding interface direction.
principles.class_reason: Mixed-script content occurs on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Do embedded paragraphs in another script carry their own language and direction?

principles.statement: Apple's symbol set is licensed for Apple platforms and integrates with Apple's system font; it is not an icon source for web products.
principles.class_reason: Using it on the web would be both a licensing problem and platform imitation; choose an openly licensed icon set instead.
principles.verification_question: Does the web product avoid shipping Apple system symbols or close redrawings of them?

principles.statement: Express brand through voice, accent color, and type while keeping standard components and letting content stay primary.
principles.class_reason: Balancing identity with familiarity is shared by HIG and Material.
principles.verification_question: Does branding ever displace content or alter a standard control's recognizable behavior?

principles.statement: Do not use launch or loading screens, or repeated logos, as branding moments that delay people.
principles.class_reason: Delays for brand display cost time on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Is there any screen whose only purpose is to show a logo?

principles.statement: Use default text sizes most people read comfortably and avoid very thin weights for body text.
principles.class_reason: HIG states sizes in Apple points per platform; on the web use a relative root size and verify at increased text size.
principles.verification_question: Is body text set in relative units at a comfortable default size and readable at 200%?

principles.statement: Build hierarchy with size, weight, and color, and keep the number of typefaces small.
principles.class_reason: Typographic hierarchy is a shared design principle.
principles.verification_question: Is visual hierarchy also expressed in heading semantics, and does the page use no more than two typefaces?

principles.statement: Apple's system typefaces are licensed for Apple platforms; the web counterpart is the system-ui stack, not a bundled copy of Apple fonts.
principles.class_reason: Shipping or imitating Apple fonts on the web is outside the no-imitation boundary.
principles.verification_question: Does the web build avoid bundling Apple system font files?

principles.statement: When text grows, keep the most important content visible and let layout reflow instead of truncating it.
principles.class_reason: Large-text resilience applies on every platform.
principles.verification_question: At the largest supported text size, is any essential label truncated or overlapped?

principles.statement: Label actions with specific verbs and keep copy short, clear, and suited to each screen's purpose.
principles.class_reason: Content design guidance is shared across HIG and Material.
principles.verification_question: Does every button or link describe the outcome of activating it, without needing surrounding context?

principles.statement: Use the same term for the same thing and the same capitalization style throughout, especially across multi-step flows.
principles.class_reason: Terminology consistency reduces errors everywhere.
principles.verification_question: Is any concept named two different ways across the flow?

principles.statement: Give every empty screen a clear next step.
principles.class_reason: Empty states occur on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Does each empty view state why it is empty and offer one action to fill it?

principles.statement: Write error messages that say what went wrong and how to fix it, in a neutral tone.
principles.class_reason: Error recovery guidance is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does each error message name the problem and a concrete correction?

principles.statement: Make every chart understandable without sight and without color, with a text summary of its key insight.
principles.class_reason: Data visualization accessibility is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Can a screen-reader user obtain the chart's main takeaway and underlying values?

principles.statement: Prefer familiar chart types and a simple default view, letting people choose to see more detail.
principles.class_reason: Progressive detail in charts is a general visualization principle.
principles.verification_question: Does the default chart answer one question, with further detail available on request?

principles.statement: Describe who can access shared content and what they can do in short, plain phrases before sharing.
principles.class_reason: Permission clarity matters on any platform.
principles.verification_question: Before sharing, can a person tell exactly who gets access and whether they can edit?

principles.statement: Offer a non-dragging way to perform anything that drag and drop can do.
principles.class_reason: Dragging is hard for many people regardless of platform.
principles.verification_question: Can every drag-and-drop outcome be achieved with single clicks or the keyboard?

principles.statement: Show whether a destination accepts the dragged item and what the drop will do.
principles.class_reason: Predictable drop outcomes are a direct-manipulation principle.
principles.verification_question: While dragging, does each potential target show whether it accepts the item?

principles.statement: Let people undo a drop, especially one that moves rather than copies.
principles.class_reason: Recoverability is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Can the last drop be undone without manual reconstruction?

principles.statement: Offer choices, defaults, and pasting instead of free text entry where possible.
principles.class_reason: Reducing typing lowers error rates everywhere.
principles.verification_question: Is any field asking people to type something the product already knows or could offer as a choice?

principles.statement: Obtain known information from the system rather than asking for it again.
principles.class_reason: HIG uses Apple system data sources; on the web expose input purpose with autocomplete tokens so browsers and password managers can fill fields.
principles.verification_question: Do personal-data fields declare the correct autocomplete token?

principles.statement: Check values as people work and make required information clear before they try to continue.
principles.class_reason: Inline validation and required-field clarity are shared form principles.
principles.verification_question: Are required fields identified before submission, and are errors reported next to the field with a fix?

principles.statement: Mask secret entry and never prefill a password field with a stored value visible to others.
principles.class_reason: Credential protection is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Are password fields masked by default, with an optional reveal control?

principles.statement: Deliver status feedback in ways every person can perceive, including assistive technology.
principles.class_reason: Status announcements are needed on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Is each success, progress, or error status announced to screen readers without moving focus?

principles.statement: Warn before an action causes unexpected, irreversible data loss.
principles.class_reason: Error prevention for destructive actions is a shared principle.
principles.verification_question: Does every irreversible destructive action require confirmation or offer undo?

principles.statement: When a command cannot run, show that it is unavailable and explain why.
principles.class_reason: Explaining constraints helps recovery on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Does a disabled or failed command tell people what condition must change?

principles.statement: Keep people's work safe automatically unless they explicitly discard it.
principles.class_reason: Data-loss prevention is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: If the tab closes or the connection drops mid-edit, is the work recoverable?

principles.statement: In full-screen views, keep essential controls reachable and let people choose when to leave.
principles.class_reason: Control over immersive views applies to the web Fullscreen API too.
principles.verification_question: In full-screen mode, are core controls reachable and does Escape always exit?

principles.statement: When people return to a full-screen experience, resume where they left off.
principles.class_reason: State restoration is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: After leaving and returning, does playback or reading resume at the previous position?

principles.statement: Show the first usable screen as quickly as possible and avoid splash screens that only delay.
principles.class_reason: Startup time matters on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Is the first meaningful content visible without an intermediate brand or splash screen?

principles.statement: Bring back the prior view, selection, and position when someone returns, so the session picks up without rework.
principles.class_reason: Continuity applies to web sessions as well.
principles.verification_question: After a reload, does the view return to the same location, filters, and selection?

principles.statement: Display available content immediately and fill in the rest as it loads.
principles.class_reason: Perceived performance principles are platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does the screen show structure or partial content before all data arrives?

principles.statement: Make clear that content is loading and, when possible, how long it will take.
principles.class_reason: Progress communication is shared with Material and WCAG status guidance.
principles.verification_question: Does every load longer than about a second show a progress indication announced to assistive technology?

principles.statement: Let people keep using other parts of the product while content loads.
principles.class_reason: Non-blocking loading is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Can people navigate elsewhere while a long load continues?

principles.statement: Let people explore before requiring registration, and explain what an account gives them when you do ask.
principles.class_reason: Deferred registration is a general usability principle.
principles.verification_question: Can a new visitor reach meaningful content before any sign-in prompt?

principles.statement: Provide an easy-to-find way to delete an account, consistent across app and website.
principles.class_reason: Account control is expected, and in some regions required, everywhere.
principles.verification_question: Can a signed-in person find and complete account deletion without contacting support?

principles.statement: Name the authentication methods that are actually available in the current context.
principles.class_reason: HIG refers to Apple biometrics and passkeys; on the web reflect what the browser and device support.
principles.verification_question: Does the sign-in screen only offer methods the current browser and device can complete?

principles.statement: Represent each notification's urgency accurately and never use urgent channels for marketing.
principles.class_reason: Trustworthy interruption is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Is any promotional message delivered through a channel reserved for time-sensitive alerts?

principles.statement: Get explicit permission for promotional notifications and let people manage notification settings inside the product.
principles.class_reason: Consent and control apply to web push too.
principles.verification_question: Can people change notification types from within the product's own settings?

principles.statement: Use modal presentation only when focusing on a short, self-contained task brings a clear benefit.
principles.class_reason: Modal overuse harms flow on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Could this modal task be done inline without losing clarity?

principles.statement: Every modal view needs a clear exit, and closing it must not silently discard work in progress.
principles.class_reason: Escape routes and data protection are platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does each modal close with a visible control and Escape, and warn before discarding unsaved input?

principles.statement: Avoid stacking modal views; close one before presenting another.
principles.class_reason: Nested modality disorients people on any platform.
principles.verification_question: Can a modal ever open another modal on top of itself?

principles.statement: Pause activities that need attention when people switch away, and resume smoothly.
principles.class_reason: HIG uses Apple app-lifecycle events; on the web use the Page Visibility API.
principles.verification_question: When the tab becomes hidden, do timers, games, and attention-requiring media pause?

principles.statement: Shape help around the tasks people perform, using consistent wording and imagery.
principles.class_reason: Task-oriented help is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Is help placed in the same location on every screen and organized by task?

principles.statement: Keep tips brief and actionable, and make them dismissible without moving focus or hiding content.
principles.class_reason: Tooltip and coach-mark behavior is shared with web guidance.
principles.verification_question: Can every tip be dismissed with Escape, and does it stay visible while hovered?

principles.statement: Teach through interaction in context rather than through long upfront tutorials.
principles.class_reason: Contextual learning is a general usability principle.
principles.verification_question: Does onboarding let people perform the real task instead of reading about it?

principles.statement: Keep any required onboarding short, make tutorials optional, and postpone nonessential setup.
principles.class_reason: Low-friction start applies everywhere.
principles.verification_question: Can a person skip onboarding and still reach the main task?

principles.statement: Respect people's silence and volume choices and never start sound unexpectedly.
principles.class_reason: HIG references the hardware silence switch and system volume; on the web avoid autoplaying audio and provide a pause or mute control.
principles.verification_question: Does any audio play automatically for more than three seconds without a control to stop it?

principles.statement: Treat haptics as optional reinforcement of feedback that is already visible.
principles.class_reason: HIG documents Apple haptic engine patterns; web vibration support is limited and must never be the only feedback channel.
principles.verification_question: Is every haptic cue paired with a visible equivalent and possible to turn off?

principles.statement: Show video at its original aspect ratio without stretching or cropping essential content.
principles.class_reason: Media fidelity is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does video keep its native aspect ratio at every container size?

principles.statement: Support the playback interactions people expect for their input device, preferring the platform's player.
principles.class_reason: HIG prefers Apple's system player; on the web prefer native media controls or a player with full keyboard support.
principles.verification_question: Can playback be started, paused, and scrubbed with the keyboard?

principles.statement: Offer printing only when output is meaningful, and keep frequently used print options separate from advanced ones.
principles.class_reason: Print relevance applies to web print styles too.
principles.verification_question: When printing is offered, does the printed output contain the content people expect without interface chrome?

principles.statement: Ask for feedback only after people have engaged, never mid-task, and not repeatedly.
principles.class_reason: Interruption cost is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Can a rating prompt appear during an unfinished task or more than once in a short period?

principles.statement: When finding things is central to the product, put search in a prominent, stable location with one entry point.
principles.class_reason: Findability is a shared navigation principle.
principles.verification_question: Is search reachable from the same location on every screen where it matters?

principles.statement: Show the current search scope and offer suggestions to reduce typing.
principles.class_reason: Scope clarity and suggestions are shared search principles.
principles.verification_question: Is the current scope visible, and are suggestion counts announced to assistive technology?

principles.statement: Consider privacy before displaying recent searches, and let people clear them.
principles.class_reason: Search history can reveal sensitive information on any device.
principles.verification_question: Can people clear search history, and is it hidden on shared surfaces?

principles.statement: Choose defaults that serve most people and keep the number of settings small.
principles.class_reason: Default quality is a general product principle.
principles.verification_question: Could any setting be removed by choosing a better default?

principles.statement: Honor system-wide preferences rather than duplicating them in product settings.
principles.class_reason: HIG refers to Apple system settings; on the web read user-preference media queries such as reduced motion, contrast, and color scheme.
principles.verification_question: Does the product read system preferences before offering its own duplicate toggles?

principles.statement: Let people adjust task-specific options where they work rather than in a distant settings area.
principles.class_reason: Contextual options reduce navigation everywhere.
principles.verification_question: Are task-specific options available from the task's own view?

principles.statement: Make undo predictable: describe what will be undone, show its result, and allow multiple steps.
principles.class_reason: Recoverability is a universal usability heuristic.
principles.verification_question: Does the undo control name the action it reverses, and can several actions be undone in order?

principles.statement: Support the platform's standard undo and redo shortcuts and avoid redefining them.
principles.class_reason: HIG names macOS menu commands and shortcuts; on the web support the host platform's conventional undo shortcuts without hijacking text-field undo.
principles.verification_question: Do the conventional undo and redo shortcuts work, including inside text fields?

principles.statement: Choose axis ranges and lower bounds that match what the data means, and use familiar tick values.
principles.class_reason: Honest axes are a general data-visualization principle.
principles.verification_question: Could the axis range exaggerate or hide the size of a change?

principles.statement: When text overlays an image, guarantee its contrast against every part of the image it can cover.
principles.class_reason: Overlay legibility is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Has overlay text been measured against the brightest and darkest regions beneath it?

principles.statement: Make a clickable image a real button or link, not a passive image with a click handler.
principles.class_reason: Role exposure is required on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Does each clickable image expose a button or link role and an accessible name?

principles.statement: Let people select and copy text that is useful outside the product.
principles.class_reason: Copyable content supports reuse everywhere.
principles.verification_question: Can people select and copy reference numbers, addresses, and error text?

principles.statement: Show the on-screen keyboard that matches the content being entered.
principles.class_reason: HIG uses Apple keyboard types; on the web use input types, inputmode, and enterkeyhint.
principles.verification_question: Do email, number, phone, and search fields bring up the matching on-screen keyboard?

principles.statement: When embedding navigable web content, support back and forward movement within it.
principles.class_reason: History navigation is expected in any embedded browser context.
principles.verification_question: Can people go back after following a link inside embedded content?

principles.statement: Give a visually grouped set of controls a short title that describes its contents.
principles.class_reason: Group labeling is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does each visual group of related fields have a programmatic group label such as a fieldset legend?

principles.statement: Prefer standard row or grid arrangements and avoid disorienting layout changes when items are inserted or removed.
principles.class_reason: Layout stability is a shared principle.
principles.verification_question: Does inserting or removing an item keep the person's place and focus?

principles.statement: Label each disclosure control with what it reveals and place it next to the content it controls.
principles.class_reason: Disclosure semantics are shared with WAI-ARIA.
principles.verification_question: Does each disclosure trigger expose its expanded state and sit adjacent to its panel?

principles.statement: Present primarily textual items as lists or tables with succinct rows and descriptive column headings.
principles.class_reason: Tabular semantics are platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Do data tables use header cells, and are list rows short enough to scan?

principles.statement: Preserve readability of long item text instead of clipping meaning through truncation.
principles.class_reason: Truncation harms comprehension everywhere.
principles.verification_question: Is the full text of any truncated row available without hovering?

principles.statement: Give clear feedback when a list item is selected.
principles.class_reason: Selection state must be perceivable on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Is the selected row visually distinct and exposed as selected to assistive technology?

principles.statement: Show hierarchy in a single leading column, make nested groups easy to expand and collapse, and use a plain table for flat data.
principles.class_reason: Tree semantics are shared with WAI-ARIA.
principles.verification_question: Is hierarchy exposed only in the first column with keyboard expand and collapse?

principles.statement: In multi-pane layouts, keep the chosen item marked in every navigation pane above the detail view.
principles.class_reason: Wayfinding in list-detail layouts is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does the list pane continue to show which item the detail pane displays?

principles.statement: Account for narrow, intermediate, and wide widths, with sensible minimum and maximum pane sizes and the option to hide a pane.
principles.class_reason: Adaptive list-detail behavior is shared with Material canonical layouts.
principles.verification_question: At a narrow width, does the split view collapse to one pane with a way back to the list?

principles.statement: Use tabs only for closely related content areas, with descriptive labels and a small number of tabs.
principles.class_reason: Tab semantics are shared with WAI-ARIA and Material.
principles.verification_question: Are tabs few, clearly labeled, and implemented with tablist semantics and arrow-key movement?

principles.statement: Controls inside a tab pane should affect only that pane.
principles.class_reason: Scope clarity is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does any control inside one tab change content in another tab?

principles.statement: Give every custom button a visible pressed state in addition to hover and focus states.
principles.class_reason: State feedback is shared with Material interaction states.
principles.verification_question: Does each custom button show distinct hover, focus, pressed, and disabled states?

principles.statement: Give the most likely action the most prominent style and keep prominent buttons few per view.
principles.class_reason: Action hierarchy is a shared principle.
principles.verification_question: Is there exactly one primary-styled button per decision point?

principles.statement: Indicate a button's role, such as destructive or cancel, through label and styling, not color alone.
principles.class_reason: Role clarity is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Is a destructive button identifiable from its label even without its color?

principles.statement: Make every context menu command also available from the main interface, and keep these menus short and relevant.
principles.class_reason: Hidden-only commands are undiscoverable on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Is each context-menu command reachable without a right-click or long press?

principles.statement: Limit submenus to one level and hide items that do not apply in a context menu.
principles.class_reason: Menu depth increases error rates everywhere.
principles.verification_question: Does any context menu nest more than one submenu level?

principles.statement: Rely on the platform's own edit commands for cut, copy, paste, and undo rather than rebuilding them.
principles.class_reason: HIG refers to Apple's system edit menu; on the web keep native selection and clipboard behavior working and add custom commands beside it.
principles.verification_question: Do native copy, paste, and selection still work wherever custom edit actions are added?

principles.statement: Label each menu item with a succinct description of its action and show when an item is unavailable.
principles.class_reason: Menu clarity is shared with WAI-ARIA and Material.
principles.verification_question: Does every menu item name its action, and are unavailable items exposed as disabled?

principles.statement: Signal when a menu command needs more input before it completes.
principles.class_reason: HIG uses a trailing ellipsis convention from Apple platforms; on the web the signal may be an ellipsis or a description, verified for clarity.
principles.verification_question: Can people predict which menu items open a further step before choosing them?

principles.statement: Use a compact single-choice control when exactly one of several options applies, and preselect a sensible value.
principles.class_reason: Single-select controls are platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does the collapsed control show the current choice so people can predict the options?

principles.statement: Group only commands related to the button's action in its menu and confirm destructive items.
principles.class_reason: Command grouping and destructive confirmation are shared principles.
principles.verification_question: Does the menu contain only related commands, and do destructive ones require confirmation?

principles.statement: The macOS menu bar is a system-owned surface with a fixed structure; web products should not draw an imitation of it.
principles.class_reason: Imitating system chrome is outside the no-imitation boundary; web command menus follow WAI-ARIA menubar semantics on their own terms.
principles.verification_question: Does the web product avoid recreating the macOS menu bar's appearance and position?

principles.statement: Choose toolbar items deliberately, move overflow into a more menu, and prefer standard controls.
principles.class_reason: Toolbar density is a shared principle.
principles.verification_question: At narrow widths, do surplus toolbar actions move into an overflow menu rather than shrinking?

principles.statement: Use placeholder hints to describe what can be searched and start showing results as people type when feasible.
principles.class_reason: Search-field behavior is shared with Material and WAI-ARIA.
principles.verification_question: Does the search field have a persistent accessible label, with the placeholder only as a hint?

principles.statement: Keep search results simple and let people filter by clearly defined scopes.
principles.class_reason: Scoped filtering is a general search principle.
principles.verification_question: Can people narrow results by category without starting a new search?

principles.statement: Keep sidebar hierarchy to about two levels, let people hide it, and group deep content with disclosure.
principles.class_reason: Navigation depth limits are shared with Material navigation drawers.
principles.verification_question: Is the sidebar a labeled navigation landmark that people can collapse?

principles.statement: Use a bottom or top navigation bar only to move between sections, never to trigger actions.
principles.class_reason: Separating navigation from commands is shared with Material navigation bars.
principles.verification_question: Does every item in the navigation bar lead to a destination rather than perform an action?

principles.statement: Keep the section navigation visible and stable, label every item, and do not hide or disable destinations.
principles.class_reason: Consistent navigation is a WCAG and Material principle.
principles.verification_question: Are navigation items labeled with text and present in the same order on every section?

principles.statement: Present a set of choices tied to an action the person started, include a way to cancel, and make destructive choices prominent.
principles.class_reason: Action-choice sheets are shared with Material bottom sheets.
principles.verification_question: Does every action sheet include a cancel path and clearly mark destructive choices?

principles.statement: Reserve alerts for critical, actionable situations; do not use them for information or for common actions that can be undone.
principles.class_reason: Alert fatigue is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Could this alert be replaced by inline status or an undo affordance?

principles.statement: Write alert titles that state the situation directly and buttons that name the outcome.
principles.class_reason: Dialog copy guidance is shared with Material.
principles.verification_question: Can someone choose correctly by reading only the alert's buttons?

principles.statement: Indicate the current position among a small ordered set of pages with simple, consistent indicators.
principles.class_reason: Position indication is shared with WAI-ARIA carousels.
principles.verification_question: Does the page indicator expose the current page and total to assistive technology?

principles.statement: Use a popover for a small amount of related content, show one at a time, and keep any work when it closes automatically.
principles.class_reason: Non-modal overlay behavior is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does opening a second popover close the first, and is input kept when a popover dismisses?

principles.statement: Make it apparent when content scrolls and support standard scrolling input including the keyboard.
principles.class_reason: Scroll discoverability is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Can a keyboard user scroll every scroll container, and is clipped content visibly hinted?

principles.statement: Avoid nesting a scroll area inside another that scrolls in the same direction.
principles.class_reason: Nested same-axis scrolling traps input on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Is there any scroll container inside another with the same scroll axis?

principles.statement: Show one sheet at a time, offer an alternative to the confirm action for dismissal, and choose a different surface for long flows.
principles.class_reason: Sheet behavior is shared with Material bottom and side sheets.
principles.verification_question: Can each sheet be dismissed without confirming, and is no second sheet stacked over it?

principles.statement: Let windows and app frames adapt fluidly to any size people choose.
principles.class_reason: Resizable frames exist on desktop web and native alike.
principles.verification_question: At every browser window width from 320 CSS px upward, does the layout remain usable?

principles.statement: Avoid drawing custom window chrome that mimics the operating system.
principles.class_reason: HIG asks apps to keep system window UI; on the web drawing imitation title bars or traffic-light buttons is platform imitation.
principles.verification_question: Does the web product avoid rendering imitation operating-system window controls?

principles.statement: Prefer the color selection UI the platform already provides over a custom picker.
principles.class_reason: HIG refers to the Apple system color picker; on the web the counterpart is the native color input.
principles.verification_question: Does a color selection field use the native color input unless a custom picker is required?

principles.statement: Prefill a combined text-and-list control with a meaningful default, label it, and offer relevant choices.
principles.class_reason: Combobox semantics are shared with WAI-ARIA.
principles.verification_question: Does the combobox have a visible label and expose its expanded state and active option?

principles.statement: State the purpose of short code entry and protect it when the code is secret.
principles.class_reason: HIG describes Apple digit-entry views; on the web use one-time-code autocomplete and a single labeled input instead of split boxes that break paste.
principles.verification_question: Can a one-time code be pasted or autofilled in one action?

principles.statement: Offer predictable, logically ordered values in place without switching views, and avoid needless precision.
principles.class_reason: Picker ordering is a general selection principle.
principles.verification_question: Are picker values in a logical order and selectable without leaving the current view?

principles.statement: Use a segmented control for a few closely related choices, with consistent segment size and either all text or all icons.
principles.class_reason: Segmented choice semantics are shared with Material segmented buttons.
principles.verification_question: Does the control have a small number of segments, exposed as a single-choice group?

principles.statement: Pair a slider with precise entry when exact values matter, give live feedback, and use the expected direction.
principles.class_reason: Slider operability is shared with WAI-ARIA and Material.
principles.verification_question: Can the slider value be set exactly with the keyboard or a text field, without dragging?

principles.statement: Make the value a stepper changes obvious and pair it with text entry for large changes.
principles.class_reason: HIG describes the Apple stepper control; the web counterpart is a spinbutton or number input with visible value.
principles.verification_question: Is the current value visible next to the stepper and announced on change?

principles.statement: Size each text field to its expected content and keep a persistent label, using placeholder text only as a hint.
principles.class_reason: Field labeling is shared with WCAG and Material.
principles.verification_question: Does every field keep its label visible while people type?

principles.statement: Make moving between fields follow the order people expect.
principles.class_reason: Focus order is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does Tab move through fields in visual reading order?

principles.statement: Use a toggle for two opposing states, identify what it controls, and make its states visually obvious.
principles.class_reason: Binary control semantics are shared with WAI-ARIA and Material.
principles.verification_question: Is the on and off state distinguishable without color and exposed as checked or unchecked?

principles.statement: Match the on-screen keyboard and its return key to the content and next step.
principles.class_reason: HIG uses Apple keyboard types and return-key labels; on the web use inputmode and enterkeyhint.
principles.verification_question: Does the on-screen keyboard's action key describe what happens next?

principles.statement: Label a gauge's current value and both ends of its range.
principles.class_reason: Range indicators need context on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Does the gauge expose its value, minimum, and maximum as text or meter semantics?

principles.statement: Prefer a determinate progress indicator, report advancement honestly, and switch from indeterminate to determinate once duration is known.
principles.class_reason: Progress honesty is shared with Material.
principles.verification_question: Does a long task show a determinate value as soon as one is known?

principles.statement: Keep a progress display visibly alive while work continues, so a running task never looks frozen.
principles.class_reason: Liveness signals are platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does a stalled task change its indicator rather than appear frozen?

principles.statement: Make ratings easy to change and keep any custom rating symbol understandable.
principles.class_reason: Rating input semantics are platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Can a rating be changed with the keyboard, and is each option named?

principles.statement: Send concise notifications without duplicates or sensitive details, and show errors inside the product rather than as notifications.
principles.class_reason: HIG describes Apple notification delivery; the same content rules apply to web push and in-page toasts.
principles.verification_question: Could any notification expose private data on a locked screen, or repeat an earlier one?

principles.statement: Use hover to preview what will happen, never to commit an action.
principles.class_reason: HIG frames this for Apple Pencil hover; the same rule applies to web pointer hover, which touch users cannot trigger.
principles.verification_question: Does any action fire on hover alone, without a click, tap, or key press?

principles.statement: Do not move focus without the person's action.
principles.class_reason: Unexpected focus changes disorient people on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Does focus ever jump without a key press, click, or explicit request?

principles.statement: Make focus move through custom views in a sensible, predictable order.
principles.class_reason: Focus order is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does keyboard focus travel through custom widgets in reading order?

principles.statement: Indicate focus with a visible appearance consistent with the platform and never let it be hidden behind other content.
principles.class_reason: HIG relies on Apple system focus effects; on the web use :focus-visible with a high-contrast indicator that is not obscured by sticky elements.
principles.verification_question: Is the focus indicator visible on every control and never covered by a sticky header or footer?

principles.statement: Offer several input routes to each action, and treat shortcut gestures as extras on top of standard controls.
principles.class_reason: Input redundancy supports people with different abilities and devices.
principles.verification_question: Is every gesture shortcut also available as a visible control?

principles.statement: Respond to standard gestures quickly and in the way people expect, and show when a gesture is unavailable.
principles.class_reason: Gesture predictability is shared with Material.
principles.verification_question: Can a person cancel a touch action by moving off the target before release?

principles.statement: Avoid custom gestures that collide with system or browser gestures.
principles.class_reason: HIG names Apple system gestures; on the web avoid capturing edge swipes, back gestures, and pinch zoom.
principles.verification_question: Does any custom gesture block browser back-swipe or pinch zoom?

principles.statement: Use device-motion input only for a tangible benefit, and always provide a conventional alternative.
principles.class_reason: Motion actuation excludes people who cannot move the device.
principles.verification_question: Can every motion-triggered action also be done with a control, and can motion input be disabled?

principles.statement: Keep standard keyboard shortcuts working and reserve custom shortcuts for the most frequent commands.
principles.class_reason: HIG lists Apple modifier conventions; on the web avoid overriding browser and assistive-technology shortcuts and let single-key shortcuts be remapped or disabled.
principles.verification_question: Does any custom shortcut override a browser or screen-reader shortcut, and can single-character shortcuts be turned off?

principles.statement: Give every shortcut a descriptive name so it can be discovered from menus or help.
principles.class_reason: Discoverability of shortcuts is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Is each shortcut listed alongside its command where people can find it?

principles.statement: Deliver a consistent experience whether people use touch, a pointer, a keyboard, or other input.
principles.class_reason: Input parity is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Does the same task succeed with touch, mouse, and keyboard alone?

principles.statement: Let people reveal controls that auto-hide by moving the pointer or focusing, and keep them visible while in use.
principles.class_reason: Auto-hidden controls must be recoverable on every platform.
principles.verification_question: Do auto-hidden controls reappear on pointer movement and on keyboard focus?

principles.statement: Let people try the product before paying and show the total price and billing period of each purchase.
principles.class_reason: HIG describes Apple's purchase system; transparent pricing applies to any web checkout or subscription.
principles.verification_question: Does every purchase option show its full price and renewal period before confirmation?

principles.statement: Apple payment buttons and marks are trademarked, system-defined artwork used only to start Apple Pay; they are not a generic payment pattern.
principles.class_reason: Using or imitating the marks outside their licensed use is brand imitation.
principles.verification_question: Does the product use official payment marks only through their official integration and never as a styling reference?

principles.statement: Keep people in control of generated output, disclose where AI is used, and keep the experience useful when generation is unavailable or declined.
principles.class_reason: Responsible generative features are a cross-platform concern.
principles.verification_question: Can people review, edit, or reject generated output, and does the product still work with the feature off?

principles.statement: Keep content current when sync is available and keep the product usable when it is not.
principles.class_reason: Offline and sync-failure resilience is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: With the network or sync service unavailable, can people still read and edit local work?

principles.statement: Make explicit feedback on automated results voluntary, describe each option plainly, and act on it promptly.
principles.class_reason: Feedback loops for automated features are platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Is giving feedback optional, and does the product visibly respond to it?

principles.statement: Make maps interactive, cluster overlapping points, and clearly identify the selected element.
principles.class_reason: Map legibility principles apply to any map surface.
principles.verification_question: Are overlapping markers clustered, and is the selected marker distinguishable without color alone?

principles.statement: Break long consent into digestible sections and confirm understanding before asking for agreement.
principles.class_reason: Informed consent design is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Is consent split into short sections, with a check that people understood before they agree?

principles.statement: Describe meaningful images and hide purely decorative ones from screen readers.
principles.class_reason: HIG names VoiceOver; the rule holds for every screen reader.
principles.verification_question: Do informative images have descriptive alternatives and decorative images empty ones?

principles.statement: Use headings, grouping, and a logical order so screen-reader users can navigate the information hierarchy.
principles.class_reason: Semantic structure is platform-neutral.
principles.verification_question: Can a screen-reader user jump between headings and landmarks to reach each section?
